articles.title: Neon sticks it to A24 by announcing a Creative Commons SCP Foundation movie
articles.summary: The studio says the movie will be in theaters next year.
articles.body: A24 pissed off one of the internet’s largest horror communities when it announced it was working on an SCP Foundation film, but apparently hadn’t bothered to contact the SCP Wiki team, nor did it commit to releasing it under a Creative Commons license as required. Seeing an easy PR win, Neon is cashing in by announcing it’s making its own SCP movie. But unlike A24, it proactively reached out to the SCP Foundation Wiki team and has pledged to release it under the Creative Commons ShareAlike (CC BY-SA) license. This is not an “official” SCP film. None of the wiki’s staff is involved in the writing or production, it is not receiving compensation, and the team’s official position is not to endorse such projects. Other than the licensing details, there is almost no information about the upcoming film. Neon says it will be released theatrically in 2027, suggesting that this will be a quick turnaround, potentially low-budget affair. That’s not shocking considering the challenges of making a profit on a film made under a ShareAlike license. In a statement, the SCP Foundation Wiki admin team said that, “The staff of the SCP Foundation Wiki and our community appreciate NEON’s excellent communication and commitment to following the requirements of our license as well as the spirit of collaboration at the core of the SCP Foundation project.“

♬ Lazzo Matumbi começa a divulgar neste mês de outubro o álbum que gravou ao vivo em 24 de julho em show apresentado na Concha Acústica do Teatro Castro Alves, em Salvador (BA), sob direção musical do maestro Ubiratan Marques.

Diretor artístico do show “Matumbi canta a Bahia”, Manno Góes é também o produtor musical e o parceiro do cantor e compositor baiano na música “Matumbi”, escolhida para abrir os trabalhos promocionais da gravação audiovisual. O single “Matumbi” será lançado amanhã, sexta-feira, 2 de outubro, com o registro dessa música que enfatiza a influência da África na cultura da Bahia.

No show “Matumbi canta a Bahia”, Lazzo celebra 45 anos de carreira solo – iniciada em 1981 com a edição de single com as músicas autorais “Salve a Jamaica (Homenagem a Bob Marley)” e “Guarajuba” – com direito a feats com BNegão, banda BaianaSystem, Coro MultiVox (sob a regência do maestro Ângelo Rafael Palma da Fonseca), a cantora Rachel Reis e o rapper Ravi Lobo.

Vocalista do grupo afro Ilê Aiyê de 1978 a 1980, período em que ficou conhecido como Lazinho do Ilê e como Lazinho Diamante Negro, Lazzo Matumbi é reconhecido no universo musical afro-baiano como uma voz ativista, importante na propagação de gêneros como samba-reggae e reggae.

Ao longo do roteiro do show “Matumbi canta a Bahia”, o cantor aborda sucessos autorais – como os reggaes “Alegria da cidade” (1988) e “14 de maio” (2021), ambos compostos por Lazzo em parceria com o poeta e compositor Jorge Portugal (1956 – 2020) – e dá voz a músicas alheias como “Brasil pandeiro” (Assis Valente, 1941), “São Salvador” (Dorival Caymmi, 1960), “Sim / Não” (Caetano Veloso, 1981), “É d'Oxum” (Gerônimo Santana e Vevé Calazans, 1985) e “Negrume da noite” (Paulinho do Reco e Cuiuba, 1989), entre outras composições.

Davidson's request was immediately met with cheers and thunderous applause from the studio audience. "You hit on something," Kimmel noted. "Look at that," Davidson said, gesturing toward the crowd. "That's the loudest response I've ever gotten," he added with a laugh. And here’s my problem with it," Davidson said. "They’re never doing anything. Someone’s just standing there eating a sandwich or on the phone, and there’s all these cones around." ZOHRAN MAMDANI ADMITS HE WANTS TO END HIS ‘ONE-SIDED BEEF’ ABOUT TAXES WITH RAPPER 50 CENT "I'm going ask him about it. I will ask him about it," Kimmel assured Davidson, who replied, "Yeah, please!" Mamdani responded by highlighting his office’s BQE Central Project, a $4 billion plan to rehabilitate the city-owned section of the Brooklyn-Queens Expressway between Atlantic Avenue and Sands Street, with construction expected to begin in 2030. "We're gonna be putting a multi-billion dollar plan to actually repair the part the city owns," Mamdani said. Barron Trump has recently debuted a more relaxed look, sporting a casual outfit and longer, tousled hair, marking a departure from his usual polished style.

Barron Trump's secret romance with a woman he met at NYU has been revealed, with reports indicating that they have been dating for over a year, as the 20-year-old navigates college life and personal relationships away from the public eye.

Melania Trump has praised her son Barron's character in her memoir, describing him as possessing a rare combination of intelligence, charm, and diligence, while also hinting at the relatable struggle she faces as he transitions into adulthood.

Barron Trump has drawn fresh attention after stepping out with a new look, marking another change from the polished style that has defined many of his public appearances.

The change comes as the 20-year-old spends more time away from the public eye, balancing college life with his growing business interests.

Barron Trump's love life also recently came under scrutiny after reports confirmed details of his girlfriend, revealing that the first son has been dating a lady he met on NYU campus for over a year now.

Barron Trump Embraces A More Relaxed Look

New photos of Barron leaving NYU show him wearing a white Ralph Lauren polo shirt with beige chinos, a brown leather belt, and a black backpack.

The outfit was noticeably more casual than the sharp suits and long wool coats he has often worn for high-profile family appearances.

His new hairdo, however, drew the most attention. Rather than the slicked-back style associated with the 20-year-old, Barron appeared with longer, tousled hair falling naturally around his forehead, as seen in images obtained by Hello! Magazine .

The change has prompted comparisons with his previous public image, although there is no indication that Barron has publicly described the transformation as a deliberate reinvention.

The latest photos follow another noticeable hairstyle change at the UFC Freedom 250 event at the White House in June.

The First Son's Secret NYU Romance Was Recently Revealed

Photos of Barron's new look come after it was reported that he's in a relationship with a woman he met in college.

The 20-year-old is said to have been quietly dating her for more than a year as attention continues to surround his personal life and recent NYU campus transfer.

Hello! Magazine reported on Sunday, September 27, that Barron is keeping the relationship largely private.

This comes amid growing interest in his dating life and his move to New York University's Stern School of Business campus in Washington, D.C.

Barron initially enrolled at NYU's Greenwich Village campus in fall 2024 and reportedly commuted to classes from Trump Tower.

According to the publication, it's unclear what the current state of Barron's relationship is, especially after his campus switch.

Meanwhile, his father, Donald Trump, previously discussed his youngest son's love life on the PBD Podcast in 2024, saying he was unsure whether Barron was "there yet" when it came to dating.

Melania Trump recently shared a new struggle dealing with an adult Barron.

Melania Trump Praised Son Barron's Character In Her Memoir

Melania Trump has previously spoken warmly about her son's personality and character.

In her 2024 memoir, "Melania," she described Barron as possessing a combination of intelligence, charm, and diligence while emphasizing his ability to remain grounded despite the upheaval surrounding his father's political career.

"Barron possesses a rare combination of intelligence, charm, and diligence," Melania wrote, according to Hello! .

She also said that he had remained firm in his character and values despite the changes and challenges that accompanied Donald Trump's election and presidency.

The comments offered a glimpse into how Melania views her son, who has grown up under an unusually high level of public scrutiny.

The First Lady Hinted At A Relatable Struggle She Has With Her Adult Son

Recently, the first lady got candid about a relatable struggle she now faces with an adult Barron. During an interview on Fox News ' "The Big Money Show," she revealed that family time with her only son was becoming less frequent.

"It's less and less family time. It's suffering because of it," Melania said, adding, "But that's OK. We are here to work, to do a good job, and that's what matters."

Speaking directly about her son, she admitted, "Barron is already a young man, so sometimes he's maybe even happy that, you know, I just want to do my stuff. And that's okay."

Barron Trump's Business Empire Is Growing

Barron has also begun developing a business empire outside the family's political world. In June, he launched SOLLOS, a beverage brand created with friends from Florida and inspired by the Sunshine State.

The company has kept Barron largely behind the scenes rather than positioning him as its public face.

Forbes also examined the Trump family's investments and earnings, highlighting cryptocurrency and international business dealings as significant sources of wealth.

The publication reported that Barron's involvement in the family's crypto ventures may have helped establish his estimated fortune at around $150 million.

Beyond that estimated net worth, Barron reportedly holds billions of cryptocurrency tokens that remain locked and cannot yet be traded. Forbes estimated that once those tokens become available, they could potentially be worth as much as $525 million.

articles.title: David Bisbal explica el motivo de su cambio de rumbo musical: “No tenía ganas de continuar con el pop actual”
articles.standfirst: El cantante fue el tercer protagonista de la semana en 'El Hormiguero', de Pablo Motos
articles.summary: El cantante fue el tercer protagonista de la semana en 'El Hormiguero', de Pablo Motos
articles.body: Este miércoles, 30 de septiembre, se emitió una nueva entrega de ‘El Hormiguero’, programa que presenta y dirige Pablo Motos en el ‘access prime time’ de Antena 3 de lunes a jueves. En esta ocasión, el invitado fue David Bisbal, reconocido cantante de nuestro país que estrena nuevo disco ‘Eternos’. El intérprete agradeció la calurosa bienvenida y se enfundó en un emotivo abrazo con el comunicador del espacio de Atresmedia. Bisbal acudió a uno de los primeros programas de Motos en sus inicios y reflexionó al respecto: “Hemos pasado muchos momentos bonitos, como pasa el tiempo”, a lo que Motos contestó: “Sigues en tu ‘prime’ como la primera visita que nos hiciste”. Del mismo modo, charlaron de su nuevo álbum de estudio, que se publica este viernes, 2 de octubre. “Estoy muy contento, hice mi gira de festivales, muy diferente, muy enérgica y en la que fui desvelando algunos singles de mi disco. Es un paréntesis que hago en el pop actual para homenajear al pop romántico castellano de los 70 o los 80”. “No tenía ganas de continuar con el pop actual y hago este homenaje a los mejores compositores, cantantes y a la industria musical de aquella época. En aquella época para que sonara una canción hacían falta 50 o 60 músicos y nosotros lo hemos grabado de la misma manera. Lo he disfrutado muchísimo y me siento un privilegiado”, añadió Bisbal en referencia a ‘Eternos’. Además, recalcó que “han respetado al 100% el sonido y el arreglo original de los productores musicales de aquella época”. Bisbal comentó que siempre quisieron respetar la melodía de los cantantes originales y que recibió mensajes de los autores de aquella época como Nino Bravo o Serrat por este décimo álbum de estudio: “Mensajes muy cariñosos. Siento respeto hoy en día, pero al mismo tiempo he decidido aprender de los más grandes”. Motos le preguntó sobre si en la gira con motivo de este álbum seguirá siendo más enérgico, a lo que reaccionó el invitado: “Paradito no voy a estar. Me pondré el smoking, pero me gusta sentir a mis músicos, a la gente, este sonido que traigo es clásico, pero no deja de ser enérgico”. Rosanna Zanetti, pareja del artista, es un apoyo para él en los momentos más adversos o antes de la salida de un disco: “Dice que siempre estoy preocupado, que soy hipocondriaco, pero siempre me abrazo a ella y le cuento todo para que me escuche, es algo que siempre hago todas las noches”. Tras ello, salió el tema de la gastronomía de Almería y Murcia a escena, sobre lo que apostilló el intérprete: “Para quitarse el sombrero”. Posteriormente, el presentador de ‘El Hormiguero’ quiso saber cómo vivió el terremoto en primera persona en Colombia. “Fue muy bestia, muy largo. Me despertó sobre las 07:30 horas de la mañana y fue muy fuerte ahora quiero ir a tener un gesto con la gente trabajó para normalizar la vida de la gente de Colombia para darles vidilla y nos acompañen en el concierto”, espetó Bisbal. Por otro lado, David Bisbal contó que lo último que cocinó fue un sándwich de doble queso y jamón york, pero que es “de poco cocinar” y “más catador que otra cosa”. Siguiendo con las preguntas personales de Trancas y Barrancas, el almeriense alegó que no le gusta llevar barba y que se afeita con cuchilla. En última instancia, reveló que “duerme de lado” y que le encanta el pistacho y la nata cuando suele comer helados.

articles.title: Alec Baldwin's civil rights lawsuit dismissed; judge cites prosecutorial immunity; calls alleged misconduct a 'very disturbing picture'
articles.summary: A US judge has dismissed Alec Baldwin's civil rights lawsuit against Santa Fe officials over the prosecution stemming from the accidental shooting death
articles.body: A US judge has dismissed Alec Baldwin's civil rights lawsuit against Santa Fe officials over the prosecution stemming from the accidental shooting death of 'Rust' cinematographer Halyna Hutchins, while acknowledging what she described as a "very disturbing picture of malicious prosecution."According to The Hollywood Reporter, US District Judge Kea Riggs ruled Wednesday that special prosecutor Kari Morrissey is protected by absolute prosecutorial immunity because the alleged misconduct occurred within the scope of her official duties.Baldwin had accused Santa Fe District Attorney Mary Carmack-Altwies and Morrissey of malicious prosecution and civil rights violations, alleging that they concealed evidence that could have vindicated him, manipulated evidence and elicited false testimony in an effort to secure his conviction.The lawsuit followed the abrupt end of Baldwin's criminal trial over Hutchins' death.As per The Hollywood Reporter, the case was derailed by a dispute involving live ammunition that retired Arizona police officer Troy Teske had turned over to the Santa Fe Sheriff's Office. The bullets were not inventoried with the 'Rust' case, meaning they were not disclosed to Baldwin or armourer Hannah Gutierrez-Reed.The court in the criminal case later found that the prosecution had "intentionally and deliberately withheld" key evidence from the defence.As per The Hollywood Reporter, Riggs also noted that Morrissey had repeatedly failed to meet discovery obligations and had given "inconsistent" testimony concerning the suppressed evidence.In dismissing Baldwin's civil claims, however, Riggs said prosecutorial immunity applies even in cases involving serious alleged misconduct."Sometimes, it is better to leave unredressed the wrongs done by an allegedly dishonest prosecutor than to subject those who try to do their duty to the constant dread of retaliation," Riggs wrote, adding, "This is one of those times."The judge added that the doctrine of absolute prosecutorial immunity can, in some circumstances, shield acts of "gross misconduct."The ruling also covers allegations involving the withholding of firearm analyses, including one analysis that identified unexplained toolmarks on the trigger mechanism of the firearm discharged on the 'Rust' set, as well as allegations that evidence was not disclosed and false testimony was given at trial.Baldwin's legal battle over the 2021 death of Hutchins has continued to draw attention. Next month, 'The Trial of Alec Baldwin', a documentary examining Hutchins' death, the ensuing media scrutiny and Baldwin's legal battle, is scheduled to open in theatres. articles.title: Linkin Park llega a los cines con 'Unshatter', el documental que muestra cómo la banda volvió a empezar tras la muerte de Chester Bennington
articles.standfirst: El documental de Linkin Park llega a los cines con imágenes inéditas de su regreso y del concierto de São Paulo de 2024
articles.summary: El documental de Linkin Park llega a los cines con imágenes inéditas de su regreso y del concierto de São Paulo de 2024
articles.body: Linkin Park ha llevado a los cines su historia de regreso con 'Unshatter', un documental que recorre el proceso que atravesó la banda después de la muerte de Chester Bennington en 2017 y los siete años de pausa que siguieron. La película, dirigida por Joe Hahn, llegó a las salas de todo el mundo el 30 de septiembre con una distribución limitada. Lejos de plantearse únicamente como una película de concierto, 'Unshatter' sigue a los integrantes de Linkin Park desde las primeras sesiones de estudio que realizaron en 2022 hasta la nueva etapa que comenzó con la incorporación de Emily Armstrong como vocalista y Colin Brittain como batería. El documental combina imágenes de archivo inéditas, escenas de los ensayos, entrevistas con los miembros de la banda y sus seguidores y actuaciones en directo. La película aborda así uno de los momentos más delicados de la historia del grupo: cómo sus integrantes intentaron encontrar una manera de continuar después de la muerte de Bennington sin limitarse a reproducir el pasado. El propio planteamiento de la cinta gira alrededor de la pérdida, la resiliencia y la reinvención artística, con la nueva formación ocupando un papel central en el relato. El proyecto estuvo inicialmente concebido como una película centrada en un concierto de Linkin Park en São Paulo, pero terminó evolucionando hacia un documental más amplio sobre la reconstrucción de la banda. Joe Hahn, miembro fundador del grupo, se encarga de la dirección y participa también en la producción. En España, 'Unshatter' comenzó a proyectarse el 30 de septiembre en diferentes cadenas y salas. Entre ellas figuran Yelmo, Cinesa, Kinépolis, mk2 y Odeon, con sesiones en Madrid y otras ciudades. Algunas salas ofrecen además pases en formatos especiales como ScreenX. El documental está estrechamente relacionado con la etapa iniciada por Linkin Park con 'From Zero', su octavo álbum de estudio, publicado en noviembre de 2024. Fue el primer disco de la banda tras el largo parón posterior a la muerte de Chester Bennington y marcó oficialmente su regreso a la actividad con Emily Armstrong y Colin Brittain incorporados a la formación. Una de las piezas centrales de 'Unshatter' es precisamente el concierto que Linkin Park ofreció en São Paulo el 15 de noviembre de 2024, dentro de su regreso a los escenarios. El directo tuvo además una importancia especial para la banda porque se celebró como parte de la presentación de la nueva etapa asociada a 'From Zero'. El concierto también ha dado lugar a un lanzamiento musical propio. El 25 de septiembre de 2026 se publicó 'Unshatter Film Soundtrack (Live in São Paulo)', un álbum en directo con 20 canciones registradas durante aquella actuación. El repertorio recorre diferentes etapas de la trayectoria de Linkin Park e incluye temas como 'Somewhere I Belong', 'The Emptiness Machine', 'Numb', 'In the End', 'Papercut' o 'Bleed It Out'.

articles.title: 32 years of 'Hum Aapke Hain Koun.':  Renuka Shahane recalls working with Madhuri Dixit, calls Salman Khan 'mischievous'
articles.summary: Three decades on, Renuka Shahane is revisiting her time on the sets of Sooraj Barjatya's 1994 hit ‘Hum Aapke Hain Koun..!’.
articles.body: Three decades on, Renuka Shahane is revisiting her time on the sets of Sooraj Barjatya's 1994 hit ‘Hum Aapke Hain Koun..!’. Now 32 years since its release, the film is still regarded as a landmark in Indian family cinema. Shahane, who portrayed Pooja Choudhury, shares what it was like to work alongside Salman Khan, Madhuri Dixit and Barjatya himself. She describes Khan as full of pranks and mischief during filming, but also speaks warmly of how generous he was toward his fellow actors.Renuka Shahane on Salman Khan and Madhuri DixitSpeaking to Variety India, Renuka Shahane opened up about her co-stars and her time on the film. On Salman Khan, she said, "Salman (Khan) was very mischievous. But he would be very appreciative of everyone when we did long takes." She was equally warm about Madhuri Dixit, noting, "Madhuri (Dixit) and I share a warm and comfortable relationship, both on and off screen. It was also a dream come true to work with her. She is one of the best co-actors I have ever worked with. I still maintain that. She is a fantastic actor."Shahane also counts her association with Rajshri Productions and Barjatya as a major milestone in her career. "I also carry memories of working with Rajshri Productions. Sooraj Barjatya is one of the finest directors," she says.Renuka Shahane on why family entertainers still matterSooraj Barjatya remains committed to the family-entertainer genre, and his next project, ‘Ye Prem Mol Liya’, will be the latest title in his filmography. Shahane feels his style of filmmaking still has takers, especially now that theatrical releases aimed at the whole family have become uncommon. "Yes, they would. People are looking for things they can see as a family. These entertainers are rare now. I am sure that they would love to go as a family. Little kids would want to go with their grandparents and watch a movie. It's a different vibe," she says.About 'Hum Aapke Hain Koun..!'Released on 5 August 1994, ‘Hum Aapke Hain Koun..!’ features Madhuri Dixit and Salman Khan in lead roles. The film is a tribute to Indian wedding customs, told through the bond between two families linked by marriage, and explores the idea of giving up one's own love for the sake of family.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.summary: Vishal Jethwa, best known for ‘Mardaani 2’ and ‘Homebound’, has made the leap from the small screen to critically praised roles in Hindi cinema.
articles.body: Vishal Jethwa, best known for ‘Mardaani 2’ and ‘Homebound’, has made the leap from the small screen to critically praised roles in Hindi cinema. He recently responded to Rupali Ganguly's observation that television actors were once treated with disdain, even though many of them now earn applause for the very same work.Vishal Jethwa on actors being labelled by platformSpeaking to The Free Press Journal at FICCI FRAMES 2026, Vishal echoed Rupali's views, saying actors often get labelled according to the medium they have worked in. Maine dekha hai ki kaafi log films mein kaam karte hain, aur unhe aisa lagta hai, 'Achha, yeh TV actor hai,' aur woh unhe categorise karte hain," he said. I've noticed that many people working in films think, 'Oh, this is a TV actor,' and they tend to categorize them.)He added, "Mujhe aisa lagta hai ki actor ko actor ki tarah dekhna chahiye, aur kisi tarah ki category nahi deni chahiye, ki yeh TV actor hai, theatre actor hai, sirf ads karta hai ya sirf modelling karta hai, aur usse zyada kaam nahi karte. articles.title: Sonali Kulkarni on playing Salman Khan's mother in 'Bharat'; 'I thought the role didn’t suit me'; reveals why she accepted it; praises Katrina Kaif
articles.summary: Sonali Kulkarni has recalled her initial hesitation about playing Salman Khan's mother in 'Bharat'.
articles.body: Sonali Kulkarni has recalled her initial hesitation about playing Salman Khan's mother in 'Bharat'. The actress revealed that she even suggested other performers for the role before eventually accepting it.The character required Sonali Kulkarni to play the mother of Salman Khan's character. She said she initially questioned whether she looked right for the part. In a conversation with Galatta India, Sonali Kulkarni explained how she responded when Ali Abbas Zafar and casting director Mukesh Chhabra approached her. She said her first reaction was to suggest other names for the character.Sonali Kulkarni questioned the castingSonali Kulkarni said she did not immediately see herself in the role. Instead, she prepared a list of actresses whom she believed could be more suitable for the character. "When Bharat was offered to me, I thought the role didn’t suit me. So, I gave director Ali and casting director Mukesh Chhabra a long list of potential actors who would look nice in the role, asking, ‘Why are you offering it to me?'”The actress stressed that she has never been particularly reluctant about taking on unconventional characters. Her filmography includes roles that required her to move far away from conventional portrayals.“I don’t have any complex about how I would play a character. I am super open about portraying any role. In my first film, Cheluvi (1992), I played a girl who can become a flowering tree. In Daayraa (1996), I played a boy with a moustache. People get scared easily when they hear that they have to play a mother’s role. But one has to keep in mind that the said mother would also be someone’s friend, sister-in-law, or wife. People remember me from Mission Kashmir (2000) as Sanjay Dutt’s wife, not simply as Hrithik Roshan’s surrogate mother.”Why Sonali Kulkarni eventually agreedSonali Kulkarni explained that the hesitation was not because she was uncomfortable portraying a mother. Her concern was whether she would physically suit the character.“So, I am not usually scared. But when it came to Bharat, I was hesitant because one should at least look the part. Then when I heard the story, I realised it emphasised more on the flashback of him as a young child. Plus, I had never worked with Salman Khan before. I met him once during the music launch of one of my films; that’s it. So, I felt this was the best way to connect with him.” The story eventually changed her perspective on the offer. The focus on Salman Khan's character during his childhood helped her understand why the casting could work.Working with Salman Khan also gave Sonali Kulkarni another reason to accept the project. She had previously met the actor only once at a film music launch.Sonali Kulkarni recalls working with Katrina KaifSonali Kulkarni also remembered her experience of working alongside Katrina Kaif in 'Bharat'. The actress specifically praised Katrina Kaif's preparation for her dance sequences. “I saw her rehearse so sincerely for her dance numbers. It was so lovely working with them.” The film marked another collaboration between Salman Khan and Ali Abbas Zafar. 'Bharat' was directed and co-written by Ali Abbas Zafar and released in 2019.'Bharat' spans several decadesThe Hindi drama follows its central character through different stages of his life. The story begins when he is eight years old and moves across several decades of India's post-Independence history. Salman Khan plays the central character, whose journey unfolds against changing social and historical circumstances. Sonali Kulkarni appears as his mother during one part of that journey.The cast also includes Katrina Kaif, Sunil Grover, Jackie Shroff, Disha Patani and Tabu. articles.title: Ringo, at 86, rocks DC, but why are we still fixated on the Beatles, six decades after their breakup?
articles.summary: The Beatles continue to captivate generations decades after their breakup.
articles.body: It was like stepping into a time machine and going back 62 years. One of the Beatles was singing rock songs, playing two instruments, making jokes and having a grand old time. The Ringo Starr concert here in Washington got me thinking about the impact that he, John, Paul and George had on the music business, the country and the culture — and how Americans are still fascinated by the Fab Four, and even their grandchildren are listening to their ancient albums. Ringo is 86 and touring again, bringing more energy to his shows than most of his Boomer-heavy audience. RINGO STARR HAS EATEN THE SAME SIMPLE SANDWICH FOR DECADES — AND IT ONLY HAS 2 INGREDIENTS Paul McCartney, who I’ve seen several times in recent years, is 84, still belting out the hits and, hip guy that he is, sharing short videos on social media. It’s not about money — the two surviving Beatles became multimillionaires back in the day. They are still releasing new albums; McCartney’s "Dungeon Lane," about growing up in Liverpool, and with him playing most of the instruments, nearly matches some of his best work. Ringo, who played drums and piano at the concert, has been saluted by today’s top drummers as having inspired generations of those behind the kit with his unique, left-handed, play-to-the-song style that doesn’t show off by overwhelming each tune. So what does this say about us as a society? It’s partly pure nostalgia, like a soup that reminds you of the way grandma made it. For those who saw the group’s American debut on Ed Sullivan and remember the frenzy of Beatlemania — with screaming girls drowning out the group — it’s a throwback to the days when they were young and groovy and often spaced out. The swinging sixties were like that — and now many of those fans now talk about medications and doctors’ visits. Some of the mystique is about the group’s incredible growth from "I Want to Hold Your Hand" to "Let It Be," with such groundbreaking records as Rubber Soul, Revolver, Sgt. Pepper, the White Album and Abbey Road. (In those days, when record players dominated our lives, music reigned because there were no Apple Watches, no TikTok, no group chats, no Netflix, no distractions from vinyl other than mediocre TV.) And it was the sheer quality launched by McCartney’s partnership with John Lennon, and its amazing variety. If you wanted hard rock, there was "Ticket to Ride," "Helter Skelter," "Come Together" and "Back in the U.S.S.R.," a Beach Boys spoof now geopolitically dated. If you preferred soft ballads, there was Yesterday, Michelle and Norwegian Wood. The Beatles had a song for every mood. There’s also a Beatles hype machine, releasing early versions of songs and old tunes, once in mono, amped up by modern technology. This enabled the other Beatles to produce three new songs from old Lennon tapes provided by Yoko. In every Beatles appearance, there was Starr and his drums on a riser behind the three guitarists, his beat driving the song but largely unnoticed by viewers and listeners. RINGO STARR REVEALS THE ONE HUMBLE RITUAL THE BEATLES REFUSED TO QUIT EVEN AT THE HEIGHT OF FAME Ringo, who was hospitalized as a boy and banged on anything that was available, got along with everyone while Paul, John and George were constantly "fussing and fighting, my friends." Consider this contrast: the Beatles' fixation is the equivalent of a focus when Ringo joined them on music from 1898. I mean, seriously? That, I think, was why I felt surging emotions at the Ringo concert. I knew I’d enjoy it; I didn’t expect to be utterly rocked, so to speak, by the drummer and his All-Star Band. And let’s be honest: With two octogenarians still cranking it out, we wonder how much longer they’ll be healthy enough to entertain us. Over the decades, the only performers who have come close to their onetime popularity are Taylor Swift and Beyoncé. For now, it was a thrill to hear Ringo belt out "With a little help from my friends." The surviving Beatles —Ringo and Paul did a duet on the Dungeon Lane album — feel like our friends. He jokingly said they could line up for handshakes after the concert. Our friends — both on our part and the former mop tops — that’s the secret ingredient.

articles.title: Noise from Universal’s latest ride made rich locals furious, fast
articles.summary: ﻿(Please don’t) scream if you wanna go faster.
articles.body: Universal Studios Hollywood has pledged to erect another sound barrier around its latest attraction after local residents complained about the bloodcurdling screams from riders. In a meeting attended by at least 350 people yesterday, park execs also promised that Fast & Furious: Hollywood Drift won’t operate between 8AM and 9AM for the rest of the year, Deadline reports. Several mitigations have already been implemented into the ride — which opened on September 16th this year — including an existing sound barrier, designing the 72 mph rollercoaster to barely make a sound during operation, and even making the rider cars turn away from the residential area during key scream moments. That hasn’t been enough, according to folks who live in the affluent nearby Toluca Lake area, and they want Universal to do more to silence enthusiastic riders. Walt Disney’s great-nephew Roy P. Disney is one such neighbor, saying “I would argue this is in violation of [Universal Studios’] land usage permits.” Another resident at the meeting complained that the noise is preventing him from composing music, and others called on execs to remember that most of their houses are older than the park (which opened as a movie studio in 1912, and became a theme park in 1964).

articles.title: Naomi Campbell’s 5-year ban on serving as a U.K. charity trustee is overturned
articles.summary: Supermodel Naomi Campbell won a legal challenge Thursday to overturn a five-year ban on serving as a charity trustee in England and Wales.
articles.body: LONDON — Supermodel Naomi Campbell won a legal challenge Thursday to overturn a five-year ban on serving as a charity trustee in England and Wales. A three-person tribunal ruled that Campbell had been “deceived” by Bianka Hellmich, a fellow trustee in the poverty charity “Fashion for Relief.” A little over a year ago, the Charity Commission, which registers and regulates charities in England and Wales, ruled that the charity Campbell founded around two decades ago was “poorly governed,” with “inadequate financial management.” It found “multiple instances of misconduct and/or mismanagement,” and that only 8.5% of the charity’s overall expenditure went on charitable grants in a six-year period from 2016. As a result, it barred Campbell from being a charity trustee in England and Wales for five years In its ruling, the tribunal confirmed there had been “serious misconduct and mismanagement” but that the “failures in the management of the charity’s finances and the misuse of its funds” resulted from Hellmich’s conduct. These, it added, were “concealed” from the 56-year-old supermodel.

articles.title: Kanye West's Russia shows cancelled after stadium row
articles.summary: Chaos has surrounded the St Petersburg shows since the stadium said it had not agreed to host the rapper.
articles.body:
Two stadium gigs in Russia by Ye, the rapper formerly known as Kanye West have officially been cancelled.

West had been due to perform at the Gazprom Arena in St Petersburg on 10 and 11 October.

But there was confusion in the lead-up to the shows, as the venue had said it wouldn't host him for what would have been the biggest show by a western artist since Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022.

In a post on messaging app Telegram, gig organisers Say Agency confirmed the concerts had been cancelled with "sincere regret".

"The Ye concerts in St Petersburg will not be able to take place on the scheduled dates," the Moscow-based agency wrote.

"We will issue an official statement regarding the status of the project and our plans in the near future."

Gazprom Arena said in August that it had not signed a rental agreement with the concert promoters and so the gig could not take place on its site.

Say Agency had said it was working to resolve the issue with the stadium before confirming they could not go ahead.

The stadium also acknowledged it had received complaints about West's performance.

He has recently apologised for multiple antisemitic and pro-Nazi comments in the past, saying he had "lost touch with reality" as a result of his bipolar disorder.

Kanye West controversies - how did we get here?

Kanye West concert in Poland cancelled over antisemitic comments

Italy bans Kanye West and Travis Scott concerts over security concerns

Russia was invaded by the Nazis in World War Two, and the country's Foreign Ministry spokeswoman was among those who criticised the planned shows.

Maria Zakharova said they were unacceptable and pointed out West's "glorification" of Hitler.

In 2025 West started selling swastika T-shirts and released a song called Heil Hitler.

Pro-war bloggers in Russia also questioned whether the country should be hosting an American artist while the US provided financial and military support for Ukraine.

West is yet to comment publicly on the cancellation.

His first major concert in the US for more than five years was held in Los Angeles in April, and he has since played in countries including Spain, Portugal and the Netherlands.

However, his Russian shows aren't the only gigs to have been cancelled.

Last summer West was set to headline London's Wireless Festival but was barred from entering the UK, forcing organisers to cancel the whole event .

West shows were also cancelled in Poland, Italy and France.

articles.title: Maths and mudras: A new chapter in the journey of rasa & rhythm
articles.summary: With hand-painted scrolls featuring dancing figurines forming the backdrop, and the mridangam and violin accompanying the measured taps of cymbals,
articles.body: With hand-painted scrolls featuring dancing figurines forming the backdrop, and the mridangam and violin accompanying the measured taps of cymbals, Bharatanatyam exponent Geeta Chandran's disciple Tara Padmanabhan began her Arangetram with a Pushpanjali at the Delhi Tamil Sangam in R K Puram recently.Years of lessons came together as she presented the traditional margam before an audience that included Prof Bijayalaxmi Nanda, Principal and Professor, Department of Political Science, Miranda House, also the chief guest for the evening, and Dr Nila Mohanan, Joint Secretary, Cabinet Secretariat, who was the Guest of Honour.The first half of the evening moved through Pushpanjali, Alarippu, Jatiswaram and a Shringara Varnam, followed by a Padam on Thaye Yashoda and concluding with a Tillana in the second half.‘Learning any of the classical forms enriches your soul’For Geeta, watching Tara take the stage was also a moment to reflect on what 11 years of learning can mean beyond the dance itself. She said, “Learning any of the classical forms is actually enriching your soul. It changes your lifestyle, approach, and thinking. This learning process inspires everything.” She added, “I am glad that Tara has stood the course and now sees value in it. All we can do is give her, and other students, that fire in the belly. The rest is their journey. In today’s time, when there are several distractions, the journey is not easy.”‘It is the start of a deeper relationship with dance’Arangetram marks the beginning of any dancer’s journey. “For me, it marks the beginning of a deeper relationship with dance – of discovering and finding new meaning in an art form that has grown with me,” said Tara, a student of BSc Mathematic at Miranda House. Her principal, Prof Bijayalaxmi, said, "Her quantitative aptitude shows in her understanding of the taal system, and even the rasa. articles.title: Amazon’s Carrie is a cyberbullying nightmare
articles.summary: Haunting of Hill House creator Mike Flanagan’s latest project is a modern reimagining of Stephen King’s Carrie.
articles.body: Do we really need a new version of Carrie? That’s the question that plagues any attempt to reimagine the classic horror tale. Stephen King’s 1974 novel remains one of his most iconic, and the film version from Brian De Palma and Sissy Spacek two years later remains unsurpassed, despite a handful adaptations that followed in the ensuing decades. Any new iteration of the story bears the burden of proving why it needs to exist in the first place. Mike Flanagan’s new Carrie series on Prime Video manages to do exactly that: It not only captures the terror and drama that has made the story so enduring, but updates it in a way that feels perfectly suited for 2026. Carrie is also notable for coming from Flanagan, who has extensive experience both with King adaptations and limited horror series. He directed King-based films like The Shining sequel Doctor Sleep and The Life of Chuck, and became especially well known for putting out a string of shows on Netflix between 2018 and 2023, including the likes of The Haunting of Bly Manor and Midnight Mass. For years he helped Netflix own the month of October, so it was something of a coup when Amazon poached Flanagan with an exclusive TV deal in 2022. Carrie is the first project to come out of that partnership. [Media: This version of Carietta White (Summer H. Howell), better known as Carrie, is a sheltered teenager who was largely isolated from the world until the death of her father. That event forced her and her mother Margaret (Samantha Sloyan) to reenter society for legal reasons, which for Carrie means attending high school for the first time. Despite a few changes here and there, Carrie tells the same basic story as its source material: A lonely young girl is met with the harsh realities of the world and is bullied to the point of awakening telekinetic powers that, ultimately, are unleashed with destructive force on a small town. The key beats remain in place, including Carrie’s most iconic scenes; Carrie is still pelted with tampons in a gym class shower when she gets her first period, and she’s still doused with pig’s blood at prom by a jealous bully. But the Amazon show, by nature of being an eight-episode series, also expands on the story. And, much like Apple TV’s recent update of Cape Fear, some of the biggest changes are down to technology. When Carrie is embarrassed in gym class, the whole thing gets filmed, which then leads to the creation of an anonymous Instagram account — handle: “carriered” — that is used to bully her and, eventually, the whole school. Unsubstantiated rumors are given life by the account, including everything from teachers dating students to popular kids getting pregnant. What starts out as a bunch of mean-spirited memes turns into real-world consequences. Margaret, who in this iteration of the story is not only a religious zealot but also a conspiracy theorist, goes on to become a “parents’ rights activist,” fighting against the account with tactics that are eerily similar to those of right-wing influencers. Flanagan is no stranger to using classic horror to explore modern issues. His final Netflix series, The Fall of the House of Usher, adapted various Edgar Allan Poe stories into a show that was ultimately about the opioid epidemic. Carrie’s modern twists feel much more natural, and smartly transform the story into one that explores just how nightmarish the high school experience has become with the advent of cyberbullying. It’s a kind of torment that follows you home, existing outside of the confines of a school, which in turn makes it that much more difficult for the school to police. Carrie is the perfect vehicle for this; she’s kind and unassuming and has little understanding of the outside world. Bullying is a confusing and terrifying experience for anyone, but its effects are heightened for an innocent kid like Carrie who simply doesn’t grasp why anyone would do this to her. She comes into the high school experience with hope and a little trepidation, and she leaves covered in blood as a town literally explodes around her. [Image: The extra runtime in Carrie is also used to flesh out some of the characters outside of Carrie herself, most notably her mother and her main bully, Christine “Chris” Hargensen (Alison Thornton). Both have moments where they’re almost sympathetic. Margaret does want to help Carrie, she just goes about it in all of the worst possible ways, while Chris is portrayed as much more than just a rich kid lashing out. She’s dealing with an extremely troubled home life and doesn’t know how to handle it. She’s mean and cruel, but you also get the sense that she wants to change, even if she can’t seem to get over that hump. The show is helped by an excellent cast — which also includes school faculty played by Matthew Lillard, Amber Midthunder, and Rahul Kohli — that make these traditionally one-dimensional characters seem like real, believable people. Almost all of the changes Carrie makes, which include some minor twists on the events of the story, are worthwhile. But there is one big exception. The show makes some heavy-handed gestures to the broader Stephen King universe of superpowered psychics — yes, at one point someone uses the word “shine” — which really starts to drag things down as it approaches its explosive finale. Not only does the addition feel unnecessary, and further complicates an already complex story, it also makes the grave error of taking away some of Carrie’s agency. I can’t say much more without delving into spoiler territory, but the change removes a lot of the punch from the finale. Aside from that, Carrie manages to answer that difficult question about why it exists. It’s not only a largely great retelling of the classic story, but one that uses that familiar tale to dig deep into an important current topic. Its modern trappings aren’t superficial twists; they heighten what was already a dark and haunting tale. And they make this iteration as terrifying as any that came before it. All episodes of Carrie will be streaming on Prime Video on October 7th.
